review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for declarations that compete with existing Mathlib, core or Batteries concepts. Most of it is lemma API (insert, singleton, pair), and I excluded standalone theorem duplicates such as `set_compr_eq_eq_singleton`, which restates `ofPred_eq_eq_singleton`. I also compared the `Unique` and `Decidable` singleton instances with the rest of Mathlib and found no competitor. The one candidate that survived is `Set.subtypeInsertEquivOption`. It overlaps `Equiv.Set.insert` in Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Set.lean, and there is a use that converts between the two. I am only moderately confident. The two equivalences have different codomains (`Option` versus `Sum … PUnit`), different decidability assumptions, and the `Option` form is used directly in the algebraic-independence files. Because `Equiv.Set.insert` lives in a later file, merging them would mean moving the definition or re-deriving one from the other, and I did not check the import graph for that. I did not check whether `Option.casesOn'` or similar API would make the Option form more convenient.

findings.excerpt:
def subtypeInsertEquivOption
    [DecidableEq α] {t : Set α} {x : α} (h : x ∉ t) :
    { i // i ∈ insert x t } ≃ Option { i // i ∈ t } where
findings.problem: This is a second, independently built equivalence between `insert x t` and `t` plus one extra point. Mathlib already has `Equiv.Set.insert`, which goes to `s ⊕ PUnit` and comes with a simp API (`insert_apply_left`, `insert_apply_right`, `insert_symm_apply_inl`, `insert_symm_apply_inr`). The `Option` version has no simp lemmas of its own. Its callers unfold the definition (`simp [Set.subtypeInsertEquivOption, ...]`). Other Mathlib code needing the same equivalence converts the other way and composes `Equiv.optionEquivSumPUnit` with `(Equiv.Set.insert has).symm` (see `linearIndepOn_insert`). Mathlib therefore has two parallel constructions of one concept, with conversions at the use sites. Finset has a third parallel version.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the `Option`-valued name, since it is used in the algebraic-independence files. Define it as a composite, `(Equiv.Set.insert h).trans (Equiv.sumPUnit-style conversion to Option)` (that is, the inverse of `Equiv.optionEquivSumPUnit`). Alternatively, state a bridging lemma `subtypeInsertEquivOption h = (Equiv.Set.insert h).trans (Equiv.optionEquivSumPUnit _).symm`. Either way, the `Equiv.Set.insert` simp lemmas could replace the ad hoc unfolding in `MvPolynomial` and `AlgebraicIndependent/Transcendental`. This probably needs the definition moved after `Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Set.lean`, or the `DecidableEq` assumption weakened to `DecidablePred (· ∈ t)`. I have not checked the import order.
findings.benefit: One source of truth for the insert-as-extension equivalence. Callers can reuse the existing simp API without unfolding definitions. The conversions in `linearIndepOn_insert` and similar proofs are no longer needed.

evidence.excerpt:
/-- If `a ∉ s`, then `insert a s` is equivalent to `s ⊕ PUnit`. -/
protected def insert {α} {s : Set.{u} α} [DecidablePred (· ∈ s)] {a : α} (H : a ∉ s) :
    (insert a s : Set α) ≃ s ⊕ PUnit.{u + 1} :=

evidence.declaration: MvPolynomial algebraic-independence proof (uses the Option version)
